candidates.summary: Laurence Tchapong failed to carry out required observations and falsified records

candidates.lead: Laurence Tchapong failed to carry out required observations and falsified records
candidates.evidence_text: Psychiatric nurse neglected patient who took own life - BBC News Image source, Merseyside Police Image caption, Tchapong was found guilty of wilful neglect By Haider Saleem Reporting from North West Published 1 September 2026 A mental health nurse who failed to check on a patient she had a "grudge" against before she took her own life has been jailed for four years. Laurence Tchapong, 54, was required to check Amy Barber, 22, every five minutes at the Brooklands psychiatric intensive care unit at Clatterbridge Hospital in Wirral, but Liverpool Crown Court heard Tchapong completed records suggesting checks had taken place on 30 June 2022. Amy was found unresponsive by a colleague but could not be saved, and CCTV showed Tchapong had not checked on her for 25 minutes. Tchapong, from Manchester, denied wilful neglect but was convicted following a trial. Image caption, Amy Barber was described as "the most caring, bright, funny girl" The Crown Prosecution Service (CPS) said Amy Barber had a complex mental health history, had been detained under the Mental Health Act and had previously displayed significant self-harming behaviour. Sentencing, Judge Murray said Tchapong had "deliberately lied" in the observation records in an attempt to evade justice. The judge said Tchapong had previously been given a verbal warning after Amy Barber photographed her sleeping and reported her to management. He said: "I am sure the defendant held a grudge against Amy for a perceived lack of warmth towards the defendant, and because Amy had previously complained about the defendant." Image source, CPS Image caption, CCTV footage of Tchapong on duty that night Reading a statement to the court, Amy Barber's mother, Susan Barber, described her daughter as "the most caring, bright, funny and intelligent girl I've ever met". She said: "She was driven. That drive was taken away by a system that let her down." She urged those responsible for patient care to "please learn from this". Tchapong told her trial the ward had been understaffed and that she had been required to undertake additional duties on the evening of Amy Barber's death. However, the judge said the jury had rejected both claims. Patrick Cassidy, defending Tchapong, said the intensity and difficult nature of mental health nursing could sometimes "wear down the resilience and the professionalism of those who operate in that sector". The court heard Tchapong had previously been of good character. Prosecutor Maqsood Khan said Tchapong had held "a position of significant trust and responsibility" but failed to carry out the checks and then sought to conceal her actions by falsifying records. candidates.summary: Michelle Pearson and her four children were all killed following a petrol bomb attack at their home
candidates.reason: Dedupe: live item has no exact/history repeat; accepted for editorial selection. | Selection: Protected item selected before size limits.

candidates.lead: Michelle Pearson and her four children were all killed following a petrol bomb attack at their home
candidates.evidence_text: Inquest to be held nearly nine years after Walkden arson murders - BBC News Image source, Family handout Image caption, Michelle Pearson, 37, and her four children were all killed following the petrol bomb attack Published 1 September 2026 An inquest is to be held into the deaths of a mother and her four children murdered in an arson attack almost nine years on from the incident. The blaze in December 2017 claimed the lives of Demi Pearson, 15, her brother Brandon, eight, and sisters Lacie, seven, and Lia, three. Their mother, Michelle Pearson, suffered 68% burns to her body and "clung on to life" until she died, aged 37, on 25 August, 2019 – 20 months after the attack in Walkden, Greater Manchester. Timothy Brennand, senior coroner for Manchester West, has set a date of 5 October for the inquest to begin. Relatives of the family believe their deaths were "wholly preventable", and have raised the question of "missed opportunities" to protect them by state agencies. Michelle Pearson had "begged" to be rehoused and called police on five occasions in the two weeks before the fatal attack, the trial of her killers heard. Zak Bolland and David Worrall were jailed for life for the attack in 2018. After a series of delays following the trial, Brennand set the inquest date in a brief hearing at Bolton Coroners' Court. The hearing was told the inquest is scheduled to last up to two months with seven police officers individually represented, along with their force Greater Manchester Police (GMP), Salford City Council, two hospital trusts, Wigan Council, Greater Manchester Fire and Rescue Service and the Independent Office for Police Conduct (IOPC). Image source, Police handout Image caption, Zak Bolland (left) and David Worrall were found guilty of the murders of Michelle Pearson and her four children The IOPC investigated the family's contact with GMP involving incidents and threats from their killers, and a report was completed in 2019, but not made public. A major safeguarding review has also been undertaken, but not made public. Bolland and Worrall were both given four life sentences and told they would serve a minimum of 40 and 37 years respectively for the petrol bombing on the Pearson family home on Jackson Street in Walkden in the early hours of 11 December 2017. Bolland's girlfriend, Courtney Brierley, 20, was jailed for 21 years for four counts of manslaughter. Bolland was present on a video-link from prison for the hearing today. Worrall, along with Brierley, no longer want to participate in the inquest, the court heard. candidates.title: Rochdale campers urged not to feed horses dangerous foods
candidates.summary: Horses in Rochdale have been given chicken bones, red onions, and lemons
candidates.reason: Dedupe: live item has no exact/history repeat; accepted for editorial selection. | Selection: Protected item selected before size limits.
candidates.practical_angle: Есть новый городской контекст для Greater Manchester.
candidates.lead: Horses in Rochdale have been given chicken bones, red onions, and lemons
candidates.evidence_text: Rochdale campers urged not to feed horses dangerous foods - BBC News Image source, Rachel Image caption, This photo was posted on Facebook to help find the collapsed horse's owner By Jade Taylorson North West Published 1 September 2026 A horse nearly died after being fed dangerous foods by campers near a farm, prompting a warning from the animal's owner. Julie Kershaw said people had been throwing unsuitable food into her field on Syke Moors in Rochdale over the summer, including chicken bones, red onions, and lemons. She is now warning people about the dangers after her horse, Frank, collapsed. "Just please don't do it because you're causing a lot of distress to the owners and the animals, and it's a lot of money – and if you can't get them right, then you've lost your pet," Julie said. Thirteen‑year-old Freya and her mother Rachel were out walking when they spotted the horse in trouble. "He just literally collapsed to the floor then went on to his side," Rachel told BBC Radio Manchester . "His breathing was really heavy and you could see his whole body shaking." Image source, Rachel Image caption, Freya has been around horses from a young age so knew how to comfort Frank Freya sat and comforted the animal before asking her mother to put an appeal on Facebook to help alert the owner. "I'm really proud of her. Within 10 minutes, Julie was on her way," Rachel said. Julie said she was "totally distressed" when she arrived. She said she was told by a vet that her horse had colitis, an inflammation of the colon, which could have spread and been fatal. "It was the worst thing. He could actually have died," she said. Image caption, Julie thanked Freya for alerting her and for staying with Frank until she arrived Freya said she was relieved to hear the horse later recovered. "I was worried and upset about him. No-one wants to see a horse in that type of state. I'm very glad that he's all right," she said. Patsy, who owns horses kept in the same area, said food being thrown into the field had been a particular problem with campers over the busy summer months. "It's been really bad this summer because it's been so warm. I've seen people standing by the horses with a chicken kebab and a naan bread," she said. "I've come to the field before and found tomatoes, red onions, lemons. Depending on what they eat, it can be really toxic to them." Julie said people think they are being kind but they should to aware that inappropriate food can make horses unwell - as can large amounts of even edible items. "It's all right to give them apples and carrots, but if 30 people come to look at the horses and they each give them an apple a day," she said. "Especially if they're overweight, it's not a good thing to do." candidates.evidence_text: Children living in temporary housing in Greater Manchester will get free bus travel to and from school on the city region's Bee Network from 1 September, mayor Bev Craig has announced The move is part of The Greater Manchester Strategy, a plan for the region's next decade which is focused on reducing the number of families and children in temporary accommodation It means children placed in temporary accommodation can always get to their school, maintaining their routine and minimising disruption to their education Families who are eligible, which includes those living more than two miles from their school or where their route is considered unsafe to walk, will be assessed for inclusion by their local council, which will then issue a pass Sam Pratt, policy and communications lead at the Shared Health Foundation, a charity that supports homeless families in Greater Manchester, said: "Families who are homelessness are struggling to pay bills, travel costs and other things while they are homeless "So actually, this new policy is absolutely ground-breaking to have extra support and extra wrap-around support for these families, and we believe that it's right to put children's education first"

candidates.summary: Residents have expressed concerns about a lack of proper consultation over the development

candidates.lead: Residents have expressed concerns about a lack of proper consultation over the development
candidates.evidence_text: Eccles: Homes will be 'completely dwarfed' by warehouses - BBC News Image source, BBC/Phil Cunliffe Image caption, Andy Spratt said residents were concerned about the scale of the development and also about what might lie beneath the ground of the former chemical plant site By Phil Cunliffe , Reporting from in Eccles and Angela Ferguson , North West Published 1 September 2026 A residents' group has expressed concern that their homes will be "completely dwarfed" by a large warehouse development being built on their doorsteps. The largest warehouse planned for the site in Eccles, Salford, is set to be 60ft (18m) high, according to nearby resident Andy Spratt. He also raised concerns about what could be in the ground at the former site of a chemical plant. A spokesperson for developer Aviva Investors said: "There is no evidence of any contamination from the previous use of the site, nor has any evidence of the presence of chemicals appeared throughout the conveyancing and survey process prior to work starting, nor since work has commenced." Plans for the brownfield site on Lankro Way, close to the Manchester Ship Canal, were granted planning permission by Salford Council in 2022. Consent was later given for Aviva Investors to build seven large storage units. Spratt and fellow resident Holly Muldoon have set up the Stop the Eccles Warehouse campaign group. Spratt told BBC North West Tonight that the end of his street and Boardman Street was "just going to be completely dwarfed by the warehouse" and could lose a lot of morning light as a result. He said it was going to be a 24/7 logistics operation "which means articulated lorries all day, all night, forklift trucks". The Mayor of Greater Manchester Bev Craig has previously said planning rules should be reviewed after complaints about warehouses being built close to people's homes. Campaigners in Astley, Wigan, have also raised concerns about the scale and proximity of a warehouse development there, as well as noise from future operations. Spratt said he was concerned about the impact of the Eccles development on house prices. "We bought our house in 2024. If we'd have known this was going ahead we wouldn't have bought it," he said. Image source, BBC/Phil Cunliffe Image caption, Holly Muldoon said she believed consultation letters had only been sent to about 70 properties when there were about 300 homes in the area Muldoon said she believed consultation letters had been sent to about 70 properties, despite the campaign group estimating the development would affect about 300 homes. She said the plans had not appeared in surveys when she bought her property in 2024. "We wouldn't have bought it if we knew that this was going to be at the bottom of the road," she said. Image source, BBC/Phil Cunliffe Image caption, Some residents have questioned why such a development can be built so close to their homes Russ Moore, whose bedroom overlooks the site, said: "It's just horrendous all day." He said dust had been getting onto his windows, window sills and cars outside. A spokesperson for Aviva said the development included a large landscaped boundary and that the application had been publicly available and subject to a formal consultation period. Image source, BBC/Phil Cunliffe Image caption, Russ Moore, whose house backs onto the site, said he was woken up by the demolition work They said they were "striving to keep any disruption to a minimum by working directly with contractors at the site to ensure the local community is kept informed on progress and that they have a point of contact should they have any concerns they wish to raise directly". "We are grateful for the patience of the local community and look forward to delivering the scheme in due course," they added. A Salford Council spokesperson said residents' concerns about the site's previous industrial use were considered and both the council and Environment Agency reviewed the contamination assessments and required conditions for further investigation, remediation and verification. "Subject to those works being completed and verified, the assessments concluded there would be no unacceptable impact in terms of contamination or human health," they added. They said residents were consulted "in line with statutory requirements, with 63 neighbouring properties notified by letter, alongside site notices and a press notice" and a wider consultation involving about 1,250 properties carried out by the developer. candidates.evidence_text: A mental health nurse who failed to check on a patient she had a "grudge" against before she took her own life has been jailed for four years Laurence Tchapong, 54, was required to check Amy Barber, 22, every five minutes at the Brooklands psychiatric intensive care unit at Clatterbridge Hospital in Wirral, but Liverpool Crown Court heard Tchapong completed records suggesting checks had taken place on 30 June 2022 Amy was found unresponsive by a colleague but could not be saved, and CCTV showed Tchapong had not checked on her for 25 minutes Tchapong, from Manchester, denied wilful neglect but was convicted following a trial The Crown Prosecution Service (CPS) said Amy Barber had a complex mental health history, had been detained under the Mental Health Act and had previously displayed significant self-harming behaviour Sentencing, Judge Murray said Tchapong had "deliberately lied" in the observation records in an attempt to evade justice

evidence_packet.evidence_text: A mental health nurse who failed to check on a patient she had a "grudge" against before she took her own life has been jailed for four years Laurence Tchapong, 54, was required to check Amy Barber, 22, every five minutes at the Brooklands psychiatric intensive care unit at Clatterbridge Hospital in Wirral, but Liverpool Crown Court heard Tchapong completed records suggesting checks had taken place on 30 June 2022 Amy was found unresponsive by a colleague but could not be saved, and CCTV showed Tchapong had not checked on her for 25 minutes Tchapong, from Manchester, denied wilful neglect but was convicted following a trial The Crown Prosecution Service (CPS) said Amy Barber had a complex mental health history, had been detained under the Mental Health Act and had previously displayed significant self-harming behaviour Sentencing, Judge Murray said Tchapong had "deliberately lied" in the observation records in an attempt to evade justice

candidates.evidence_text: Oldham Hidden beauty spot powered Greater Manchester's revolution but nobody talks about it The site powered Manchester’s industrial revolution and was the site of illegal raves attended by thousands in 2020 Comments News Edward Barnes Local Democracy ‘Ambitious’ plans to restore a major wildlife area next to the M60 are about to take another step forward. The attraction, which ‘no one talks about’ locally, is already bringing in people from across the country Daisy Nook Country Park is a 40 hectare site in the River Medlock valley which sits in both Oldham and Tameside boroughs. Daisy Nook’s history stretches back over 200 years where the canals there acted as a key supplier of coal that powered Manchester’s industrial revolution and The area is known for its beautiful scenery, wildlife, and waterways and is popular with photographers. Later this month, the Friends of Daisy Nook Country Park are set to formally sign an agreement on September 11 to help move an ‘ambitious’ community led programme forward Working with the Hollinwood Canal Society, this will look to restore and regenerate the park. £120,000 of funds is set to be spent over the coming months which will help restore sections of the historic canal and a former boat pond This is on top of work since 2024 to improve paths, create community spaces, tackle invasive species like Japanese knotweed and Himalayan balsam, improve accessibility, and carry out repairs

Traffic has already been widely impacted with delays along Hough Lane and other nearby roads Buses are still running along the route as the closure is to 'allow essential utility works as part of the new Tyldesley travel hub, which will add an extra 99 parking bays at the site, aiming to address concerns from residents and local traders about on-street parking in the tow A letter from Transport for Greater Manchester to residents living nearby said: “As part of the next phase of construction, Astley Street will be closed to vehicles immediately north of the guided busway from August 31 to September 14." The existing park and ride facility remains open and bus services are running as usual, but there are concerns about the disruption the road closure is causing and questions over why it's happening on the week children return to school for the new academic year

candidates.evidence_text: Bury African police officer 'a clear victim of bullying' as gross misconduct against GMP cops found proven PC Mohammed Abid found to have directed a 'racist comment' towards her about her hair View 3 Images Bury police station (Image: Jason Roberts /M News Paul Britton Reporter 16:30, 01 Sep 2026 Updated 16:30, 01 Sep 2026 The mocking and mimicking of a black female police officer's African accent at work by five officers and two now former officers who were her colleagues was gross misconduct, a misconduct panel has ruled The constable was, said the chair of the misconduct hearing, a 'clear victim of bullying' Another officer - PC Mohammed Abid - was also found to have directed a 'racist comment' towards her about her hair, describing it as 'looking like a mop, before smiling and walking away'. His actions, too, amounted to gross misconduct, the panel ruled Misconduct, but not gross misconduct, was found to be proven against a ninth officer, Sergeant Adrian Bick. A misconduct hearing was told Sgt Bick compared an image of a suspect he was shown by one of the five officers to the African officer's mother Delivering his findings on Tuesday (September 1), the panel's chair Assistant Chief Officer Jonathan Roy said he found there was a 'culture of mocking accents' within the police unit at Bury police station, where they were all based

candidates.lead: But bigger is not always better.
candidates.evidence_text: But bigger is not always better. And not long after last year’s event, the company behind what had been known as Manchester Pride went into voluntary liquidation Bosses said the event was no longer “financially viable” due to rising costs and lower ticket sales. It was the headline and local performers as well as suppliers and staff who lost out - and many have yet to be paid for their services With the future of the festival in jeopardy, a group of Village stalwarts put themselves forward, joined forces with Manchester Council and the Equity union and created a Community Interest Company (CIC) to create the inaugural Manchester Village Pride View 8 Images People enjoying Manchester Village Pride (Image: Sean Hansford | Manchester Evening News) The focus has been on reengaging with the original intentions of the Pride movement. And many of those attending told our reporters that the changes are for the better . A ‘quieter’, ‘calmer’ Pride focussed on community Tens of thousands attended to watch Cleopatra, B*Witched, DJ Sammy, Cascada, Kate Nash and Gareth Gates. “I think its actually better,” said Mark Doyle, from Hulme

candidates.evidence_text: Oldham Hidden beauty spot powered Greater Manchester's revolution but nobody talks about it The site powered Manchester’s industrial revolution and was the site of illegal raves attended by thousands in 2020 Comments News Edward Barnes Local Democracy ‘Ambitious’ plans to restore a major wildlife area next to the M60 are about to take another step forward. The attraction, which ‘no one talks about’ locally, is already bringing in people from across the country Daisy Nook Country Park is a 40 hectare site in the River Medlock valley which sits in both Oldham and Tameside boroughs. Daisy Nook’s history stretches back over 200 years where the canals there acted as a key supplier of coal that powered Manchester’s industrial revolution and The area is known for its beautiful scenery, wildlife, and waterways and is popular with photographers. Later this month, the Friends of Daisy Nook Country Park are set to formally sign an agreement on September 11 to help move an ‘ambitious’ community led programme forward Working with the Hollinwood Canal Society, this will look to restore and regenerate the park. £120,000 of funds is set to be spent over the coming months which will help restore sections of the historic canal and a former boat pond This is on top of work since 2024 to improve paths, create community spaces, tackle invasive species like Japanese knotweed and Himalayan balsam, improve accessibility, and carry out repairs

candidates.evidence_text: Traffic and travel Once you pop, you get stopped - car seized for what driver did while passing cops The driver was promptly hit with a traffic offence Comments News Greta Simpson Senior Reporter 20:39, 01 Sep 2026 View Image A BMW was seized on Princ A driver who made their car 'pop and bang' as they passed by police officers in south Manchester promptly had their vehicle seized, Greater Manchester Police has said The Chorlton and Didsbury district shared a photo of what appears to be a blue BMW x5 in the process of being loaded onto a trailer on the side of Princess Parkway, near to the junction with Mauldeth Road West The force said they had been dealing with an incident near to the junction of Princess Road and Moss Lane East when a passing car caught their attention The driver reportedly slowed down while passing officers, before making the car 'pop and bang' before accelerating away They were subsequently hit with a traffic offence report and the vehicle was subsequently seized

candidates.evidence_text: Manchester Pride Police praise Manchester Pride as 17 people arrested mostly for drug crimes Police aimed to make the festival 'the safest it can be' News John Scheerhout Crime reporter 18:13, 01 Sep 2026 Updated 18:14, 01 Sep 2026 View 3 Images There A police boss has praised Manchester's Pride festival with just 17 people arrested during the bank holiday extravaganza Some 30,000 people attended the celebration across the weekend, concluding with a candlelight vigil on Monday night. Policed drafted in extra officers to the city centre as well as drones and drugs sniffer dogs to make the festival 'the safest it can be' Today Assistant Chief Constable Matt Boyle, of GMP, praised the security around the celebration after he revealed just 17 people were arrested, most for drugs offences Drugs sniffer dogs, named Max and Doodle, also helped officers make 15 drugs finds, resulting in the arrest of one man, 22, on suspicion of possession with intent to supply drugs The suspect was found with a large bottle of what is believed to be GHB or GBL, Viagra and lubricant, according to GMP. He has been released on bail with 'stringent conditions' as an investigation continues

candidates.evidence_text: Manchester City Centre Drivers stuck in city centre for hours on end by Pride road closures slam 'poor planning' 'An event cannot trap people like this' Comments News Greta Simpson Senior Reporter 18:00, 01 Sep 2026 Updated 18:00, 01 Sep 2026 View 3 I Drivers have slammed the traffic management of Manchester Village Pride after they reported being trapped in their cars for more than four hours in Manchester city centre on Saturday (August 30) The parade, which was attended by thousands of marchers and revellers despite intermittent downpour throughout the day, meant that extensive road closures were in place, including around Deansgate These were made public in the days leading up to the event, alongside several bus lane suspensions on Bridge Street, Whitworth Street West and Portland Street But motorists that were caught up in the closures have slammed the event management as 'chaos' after they reported being stuck on the gridlocked roads for hours at a time on Saturday afternoon Simon Weiner had driven into the city centre from Cheetham Hill to meet a friend for brunch. Intending to head south to Trafford Park afterwards, he said they saw 'loads of traffic' on Deansgate so turned left onto Hardman Street near Spinningfields at around 11:45am

candidates.evidence_text: Manchester Manchester skatepark branded ‘unsafe’ after event which descended into chaos Details were shared in a licensing hearing. Comments News Declan Carey Local Democracy Reporter 17:36, 01 Sep 2026 View 2 Images Pictures were shared in a council An event at a Manchester skatepark was slammed for being ‘unsafe’ after descending into chaos with people ‘scaling fences’ and ‘forcibly pulling apart barriers’ Projekts MCR hosted an externally promoted music event on May 29 based at its skatepark located under the Mancunian Way It was planned to hold up to 1,000 guests but more than 2,000 tickets were issued in total, leading to ‘large crowds’ of people turning up in scenes which ‘very quickly proved to be dangerous’ Greater Manchester Police (GMP) said the event was ‘poorly planned, poorly managed, and unsafe’ for those who turned up, while the council’s licensing and out of hours team said the event led to noise complaints Details from the event were shared at a Manchester council licensing meeting on Tuesday (September 1)

candidates.evidence_text: But bigger is not always better. And not long after last year’s event, the company behind what had been known as Manchester Pride went into voluntary liquidation Bosses said the event was no longer “financially viable” due to rising costs and lower ticket sales. It was the headline and local performers as well as suppliers and staff who lost out - and many have yet to be paid for their services With the future of the festival in jeopardy, a group of Village stalwarts put themselves forward, joined forces with Manchester Council and the Equity union and created a Community Interest Company (CIC) to create the inaugural Manchester Village Pride View 8 Images People enjoying Manchester Village Pride (Image: Sean Hansford | Manchester Evening News) The focus has been on reengaging with the original intentions of the Pride movement. And many of those attending told our reporters that the changes are for the better . A ‘quieter’, ‘calmer’ Pride focussed on community Tens of thousands attended to watch Cleopatra, B*Witched, DJ Sammy, Cascada, Kate Nash and Gareth Gates. “I think its actually better,” said Mark Doyle, from Hulme

The attraction, which ‘no one talks about’ locally, is already bringing in people from across the country Daisy Nook Country Park is a 40 hectare site in the River Medlock valley which sits in both Oldham and Tameside boroughs. Daisy Nook’s history stretches back over 200 years where the canals there acted as a key supplier of coal that powered Manchester’s industrial revolution and The area is known for its beautiful scenery, wildlife, and waterways and is popular with photographers. Later this month, the Friends of Daisy Nook Country Park are set to formally sign an agreement on September 11 to help move an ‘ambitious’ community led programme forward Working with the Hollinwood Canal Society, this will look to restore and regenerate the park. £120,000 of funds is set to be spent over the coming months which will help restore sections of the historic canal and a former boat pond This is on top of work since 2024 to improve paths, create community spaces, tackle invasive species like Japanese knotweed and Himalayan balsam, improve accessibility, and carry out repairs

Buckley returned to crime on November 25. At around 7.30pm on that date, Buckley encountered a man who was renting a “He met the defendant on the shared stairs,” prosecutor Andrew Evans told Carlisle Crown Court on Tuesday, September 1. “He asked what she was doing there and was told that she was waiting for the occupant of the neighbouring room "He told her he wasn’t usually home until 10 and sometimes not at all, but she decided to wait. He went into his own room, but when he stepped out again four hours later she was still there “He offered to make her a coffee, and went into the kitchen. candidates.evidence_text: Leigh Guided Busway Major road closed as Tyldesley residents face fortnight of disruption Drivers have been warned to expect delays Comments News Emma Gill Parents editor 18:45, 01 Sep 2026 Updated 19:24, 01 Sep 2026 View 4 Images Astley Street in Tyl One of Tyldesley's busiest roads has shut completely for two weeks as works are carried out on a new travel hub Drivers have been warned to expect delays as Astley Street is closed in both directions close to Leigh Guided Busway until the middle of September. Traffic has already been widely impacted with delays along Hough Lane and other nearby roads Buses are still running along the route as the closure is to 'allow essential utility works as part of the new Tyldesley travel hub, which will add an extra 99 parking bays at the site, aiming to address concerns from residents and local traders about on-street parking in the tow A letter from Transport for Greater Manchester to residents living nearby said: “As part of the next phase of construction, Astley Street will be closed to vehicles immediately north of the guided busway from August 31 to September 14." The existing park and ride facility remains open and bus services are running as usual, but there are concerns about the disruption the road closure is causing and questions over why it's happening on the week children return to school for the new academic year

candidates.evidence_text: Bolton Plans to charge for parking at beauty spot gifted to the public for ‘free and uninterrupted enjoyment’ put on hold United Utilities, who manage Lever Park said it will now ‘review and reshape' the controversial plans Comments News Chris Gee Loc Plans to introduce parking charges at a beloved tourist destination have been put on hold after a wave of opposition United Utilities planned to charge motorists to park at various points around Lever Park in the Rivington area, widely appreciated in the region for its natural beauty The company has withdrawn a series of planning application to install ANPR cameras following ‘concerns raised by local people and recognise that further consultation is needed’ The utility company said it will now ‘review and reshape our plans’ The vast park, which welcomes hundreds of thousands of visitors from across the north west and further afield each year includes reservoirs, hillside walks, Rivington Pike and the ruins of Lord Leverhulme’s terraced gardens, known to locals as the Chinese Gardens

candidates.evidence_text: Manchester synagogue attack 'I understand why Jewish people feel very frightened', GMP chief says at memorial for synagogue terror attack victims GMP Chief Constable vowed to 'bend every sinew' to fight antisemitism View 2 Images GMP Chief Constable S News Damon Wilkinson Reporter 19:14, 01 Sep 2026 Greater Manchester Police Chief Constable Sir Stephen Watson said he understands why Jewish people in Greater Manchester feel frightened in the wake of the Heaton Park synagogue attack and other antisemitic atrocities around the wo Speaking to the Manchester Evening News on Monday night (August 31) ahead of a memorial at the Crumpsall synagogue GMP's Chief Constable said he 'regrets' the fact Jewish people feel less safe Responding to earlier remarks made by Heaton Park Rabbi Daniel Walker - who said the community feels more vulnerable now than it did at the time of the attack - Sir Stephen said: "The fact that people feel more fearful post a terrorist attack on the steps of this very synagogue j "And of course I regret the fact that people feel less safe, but one only has to look at the litany of terrorist atrocities, both in the UK and abroad. You've seen the fact that we are prosecuting people who have conspired with the terrorist who committed this attack and assisted "All of this adds to this community feeling very frightened and I understand that. What we have to do, of course, is to bend every sinew to reduce threat, risk and harm and that is what we are determined to do."

candidates.evidence_text: Manchester Pride Police praise Manchester Pride as 17 people arrested mostly for drug crimes Police aimed to make the festival 'the safest it can be' News John Scheerhout Crime reporter 18:13, 01 Sep 2026 Updated 18:14, 01 Sep 2026 View 3 Images There A police boss has praised Manchester's Pride festival with just 17 people arrested during the bank holiday extravaganza Some 30,000 people attended the celebration across the weekend, concluding with a candlelight vigil on Monday night. Policed drafted in extra officers to the city centre as well as drones and drugs sniffer dogs to make the festival 'the safest it can be' Today Assistant Chief Constable Matt Boyle, of GMP, praised the security around the celebration after he revealed just 17 people were arrested, most for drugs offences Drugs sniffer dogs, named Max and Doodle, also helped officers make 15 drugs finds, resulting in the arrest of one man, 22, on suspicion of possession with intent to supply drugs The suspect was found with a large bottle of what is believed to be GHB or GBL, Viagra and lubricant, according to GMP. He has been released on bail with 'stringent conditions' as an investigation continues

He has been released on bail with 'stringent conditions' as an investigation continues

candidates.evidence_text: Manchester Manchester skatepark branded ‘unsafe’ after event which descended into chaos Details were shared in a licensing hearing. Comments News Declan Carey Local Democracy Reporter 17:36, 01 Sep 2026 View 2 Images Pictures were shared in a council An event at a Manchester skatepark was slammed for being ‘unsafe’ after descending into chaos with people ‘scaling fences’ and ‘forcibly pulling apart barriers’ Projekts MCR hosted an externally promoted music event on May 29 based at its skatepark located under the Mancunian Way It was planned to hold up to 1,000 guests but more than 2,000 tickets were issued in total, leading to ‘large crowds’ of people turning up in scenes which ‘very quickly proved to be dangerous’ Greater Manchester Police (GMP) said the event was ‘poorly planned, poorly managed, and unsafe’ for those who turned up, while the council’s licensing and out of hours team said the event led to noise complaints Details from the event were shared at a Manchester council licensing meeting on Tuesday (September 1)

"He does now."

candidates.summary: Bury African police officer 'a clear victim of bullying' as gross misconduct against GMP cops found proven PC Mohammed Abid found to have directed a 'racist comment' towards her about her hair View 3 Images Bury police station (Image: Jason Roberts /M News Paul Britton Reporter 1

candidates.lead: Bury African police officer 'a clear victim of bullying' as gross misconduct against GMP cops found proven PC Mohammed Abid found to have directed a 'racist comment' towards her about her hair View 3 Images Bury police station (Image: Jason Roberts /M News Paul Britton Reporter 1
candidates.evidence_text: Bury African police officer 'a clear victim of bullying' as gross misconduct against GMP cops found proven PC Mohammed Abid found to have directed a 'racist comment' towards her about her hair View 3 Images Bury police station (Image: Jason Roberts /M News Paul Britton Reporter 16:30, 01 Sep 2026 Updated 16:30, 01 Sep 2026 The mocking and mimicking of a black female police officer's African accent at work by five officers and two now former officers who were her colleagues was gross misconduct, a misconduct panel has ruled The constable was, said the chair of the misconduct hearing, a 'clear victim of bullying' Another officer - PC Mohammed Abid - was also found to have directed a 'racist comment' towards her about her hair, describing it as 'looking like a mop, before smiling and walking away'. His actions, too, amounted to gross misconduct, the panel ruled Misconduct, but not gross misconduct, was found to be proven against a ninth officer, Sergeant Adrian Bick. A misconduct hearing was told Sgt Bick compared an image of a suspect he was shown by one of the five officers to the African officer's mother Delivering his findings on Tuesday (September 1), the panel's chair Assistant Chief Officer Jonathan Roy said he found there was a 'culture of mocking accents' within the police unit at Bury police station, where they were all based

candidates.title: The Mancunian Way: Same name, very different vibe
candidates.summary: But bigger is not always better. And not long after last year’s event, the company behind what had been known as Manchester Pride went into voluntary liquidation Bosses said the event was no longer “financially viable” due to rising costs and lower ticket sales

candidates.lead: But bigger is not always better.
candidates.evidence_text: But bigger is not always better. And not long after last year’s event, the company behind what had been known as Manchester Pride went into voluntary liquidation Bosses said the event was no longer “financially viable” due to rising costs and lower ticket sales. It was the headline and local performers as well as suppliers and staff who lost out - and many have yet to be paid for their services With the future of the festival in jeopardy, a group of Village stalwarts put themselves forward, joined forces with Manchester Council and the Equity union and created a Community Interest Company (CIC) to create the inaugural Manchester Village Pride View 8 Images People enjoying Manchester Village Pride (Image: Sean Hansford | Manchester Evening News) The focus has been on reengaging with the original intentions of the Pride movement. And many of those attending told our reporters that the changes are for the better . A ‘quieter’, ‘calmer’ Pride focussed on community Tens of thousands attended to watch Cleopatra, B*Witched, DJ Sammy, Cascada, Kate Nash and Gareth Gates. “I think its actually better,” said Mark Doyle, from Hulme

It was the first business to move into Astley Business Park, a PLP development dogged by issues since construction started more than a year ago. So Since 24-hour operations - including numerous HGV movements - began, nearby households have reported issues about noise, with some complaining of sleep disturbance, banging and background hum. The company has now agreed to cease overnight transport operations between midnight and The Astley Warehouse Action Group recently commissioned a noise report which claimed levels were above thresholds. It said ‘residents have been woken throughout the night since Whistl opened’ and ‘six hours of guaranteed respite will make some difference’ Whistl has now acknowledged ‘that our operations at PLP Astley have had an impact on nearby residents, particularly in relation to night-time noise’. They added that ‘we take those concerns very seriously’

He sadly died of his injuries later that day How far he fell hasn't been confirmed, but specialist scenes of crime investigators were pictured inside the flats on Saturday morning working on a top-floor balcony. Following his death, Shay's friends paid tribute to him on social media

candidates.evidence_text: Real Life Manchester student, 21, put leg pains down to gym workouts, then saw shock diagnosis on NHS app "I couldn’t really process it straight away" Comments News Ria Newman and Ashlie Blakey Live and breaking news reporter 08:19, 01 Sep 2026 View 6 A Manchester student put his leg pain down to his gym workouts for three years before he was diagnosed with a rare cancer Cian Douglas frequently worked out at the gym and put his aches and pains down to exercise. The 21-year-old visited doctors twice, who thought he was suffering from possible nerve damage Years later after a number of scans and tests, he was diagnosed with synovial sarcoma – a rare soft tissue cancer that develops from an abnormal gene swap between chromosomes. Cian said he received the shock diagnosis on the NHS app while in Starbucks with his mum Louise “It was a complete shock,” Cian told NeedToKnow . "It instantly sent so many emotions racing through my mind – mostly grief, sadness, and fear. I couldn’t really process it straight away.” When they arrived for the formal diagnosis in-person, Cian said doctors apologised for the mishap, and moved on to discussing treatment options for the young man. He has since undergone seven surgeries and has had to learn how to walk again

Credit: ITV News Reform UK and Labour have gone through to the second round of voting in the Greater Manchester Mayoral by-ele Neither Labour's Bev Craig or Reform UK's Sian Astley managed to secure a majority, meaning voters second choice ballots will now be counted to decide an overall winner Five candidates have now been eliminated from the contest to become Greater Manchester mayor – Geraldine Coggins (Green), Phil Eckersley (Conservative), Marcus Farmer (Independent), Richard Kilpatrick (Liberal Democrats) and Marlon West (Restore Britain) The by-election is using a voting system called supplementary vote (SV), which sees voters mark their ballot papers with a first and second choice, and if any candidate wins more than 50% of the first-choice votes, they are declared the winner That has not happened in Greater Manchester, so the top two candidates, Labour’s Bev Craig and Reform UK candidate Sian Astley, move to a second round ITV Granada Reports' Political Correspondent Lise McNally sent the latest from the Co-op Live as counting for the second round got underway

Officers spoke to those at the encampment, who said they intended to leave by Saturday 8th August As the site had not been vacated, the Council returned with support from Greater Manchester Police on Tuesday 11th August. A formal direction was served under Section 77 of the Criminal Justice and Public Order Act 1994, requiring those at the encampment to leave and remove their The Council also provided information about authorised sites in Greater Manchester, along with advice about health, wellbeing and reporting hate crime After the direction was not followed, the Council began court proceedings. On Monday 17th August, Tameside Magistrates’ Court granted an order requiring the removal of the encampment The site was vacated later that day. The gank was characterised by tightly packed housing, narrow passageways, high crime rates and large numbers of ‘ The site is so steep that Oldham contractors, Maysand, who delivered the work, had to devise a special pulley system with tracks and rollers to help transport the stone up the hill The team had to painstakingly remove all 122 steps, many of which had become broken and uneven, before reconstructing both the area underneath and the damaged steps using traditional sandstone, to match the existing stone. candidates.evidence_text: Experience the raw, unfiltered power of Balkan folklore in a new immersive show from the world’s most famous performance artist Balkan Erotic Epic is a bold new performance work created by the iconic artist Marina Abramović . Regarded as the world’s most influential performance artist, Abramović’s transformative work has reached millions of people – from opening the Pyramid Stage at Glastonbury Festival t A four-hour ritual where ancient myth meets performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic explores the eroticism, spirituality and traditions of Abramović’s homeland through 13 visceral scenes Brought to life by a cast of over 70 performers, dancers, musicians and singers, the experience unfolds across Aviva Studios. Audiences are free to choose their own path – with pop-up encounters punctuating the action, bringing bodies together in dance, song and ritual Watch Fertility Rite , a fevered ritual where bodies writhe against the ground in a desperate call for fertility. Witness Massaging the Breast where women gesticulate over graves to awaken the earth. In Scaring the Gods , women bare themselves to the sky to banish storms. Listen Unafraid to push the boundaries of eroticism and performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic asks its audience a timeless question: What are our bodies truly for?

candidates.evidence_text: Grub on the Docks - Media City UK Street Food Line-Up: Featuring Sizzling Seoul, Dukes Po Boys, and more Grub on the Docks Venue Gardens Dates 28 th May - 20 th Sep '26 Open Tuesday to Sunday weekly, 12 noon – 10pm GRUB on the Docks is bringing the flavour this summer – think unreal street food, ice-cold drinks and non-stop vibes right in the MediaCity gardens, on the waterfront. We’re talking a stacked rotation of indie food like Sizzling Seoul, Umami Cartel, Oppa Korean Dogs and more, switching it up every week so there’s always something new to try. NEW challenge, take on the BELLY BUSTER CHALLENGE from CAFF – sausage. bacon. egg. black pudding. hash brown. All packed into one proper Belly Buster bap for £7.50. Time to beat is 5 minutes set the fastest finishing time and your next Belly Buster is FREE . EVENTS Wine on the Docks Every Wednesday | All day, venue hours Midweek just got better. Every Wednesday, buy two glasses of the same wine and we’ll top up the rest of the bottle on us. No catch, no fuss just a proper reason to make Wednesday your new favourite day. Sunset Sessions Every Friday | 5–8pm Clock off and head straight to the water’s edge. A rotating line-up of DJs kicks off the weekend early, with a trader special and a featured drinks offer to match. Same time, same spot, every Friday, your after-work wind-down sorted. Paws on the Docks 8 AUGUST | 22 AUGUST | 5 SEPTEMBER | 19 SEPTEMBER | Mornings Bring the dog, grab a coffee, make a morning of it. Paws on the Docks is our relaxed dog-friendly social – think breakfast specials, water bowls, complimentary pup cups and market stalls that welcome four-legged visitors as warmly as the two-legged ones. Residents social Thursday 20th August – 5pm to 7pm An evening for all MediaCity residents, with a DJ playing live on the docks. A nice informal social, come down, grab a drink and meet other residents at our waterfront setting. Media Makers Mixer Thursday 27th August – 5pm to 7pm A regular hosted networking event for MediaCity’s creative and production community, designed to bring people together and encourage connections across the area. Be the first in the know Sign up to receive email updates on the latest events, news and offers at MediaCity Visit our privacy policy here. This Autumn her new exhibition, Just a Girl from North Manchester, lands at Manchester Central Library. Including a collection of black and white photographs with a focus on musicians, communities and everyday moments that would otherwise have been forgotten, the exhibition provides a journey through Manchester’s musical and cultural history. Home to two of the most renowned clubs in British sport - Manchester United and Lancashire County Cricket Club , The Quays is the area to head for when wanting the best in football and cricket. Both have official sh Built in 2000 at the booming Salford Quays, this astonishing building is a shrine to all things art, with galleries, theatres, workshops, cafes and shops. It's worth a visit just to sit outside and admire the vision in metal and glass. But you'd be missing out on a whole world of Watersports The Salford Watersports Centre at The Quays is a unique sporting venue which is well placed and perfect for taking to the water. It already has a strong tech base and devolution gives us a chance to align policy, funding and delivery more closely with what is happening on the ground To do that well, Combined Authorities and others need to understand that ecosystems are much broader and deeper than most public-facing institutions realise, that matters if they are going to make good decisions on skills, infrastructure, procurement and innovation support AI and emerging technologies clearly need focus because their impact will be felt across every part of the economy, but policy needs to keep pace with how those technologies are being used by businesses. Government and Combined Authorities will have more impact if they understand The new Digital Campus in Manchester is a good example of where this could become practical; a larger concentration of public sector digital capability in Manchester should create new routes for startups and scaleups to work with the government. evidence_packet.evidence_text: The best industry experiences don’t just show young people what a career in tech could look like - they give them the opportunity to become part of it That’s exactly what Hippo helped create through their support of Manchester Digital’s T Connect programme, providing students with exposure to the industry, practical experience and the confidence to take their next steps into tech Hippo’s involvement began with a problem-solving session for T Connect students, where their team ran activities designed to encourage creative thinking, collaboration and approaching challenges in the way technology teams do every day Following this session, Hippo selected two learners - Ahmed Abdul Karim and Edu Samuel Manuel - to take part in a 36-day industry placement with the business The placement gave Ahmed and Edu the opportunity to work alongside Hippo’s teams from their Leeds office, contributing to projects for the Department for Education and gaining first-hand experience of working in a professional technology environment Throughout their placements, they were treated as members of the team, gaining insight into the full process of delivering digital products - from technical development and problem solving through to collaboration and communication

candidates.lead: A Salford motion capture startup has been bought by Oxford Metrics plc.
candidates.evidence_text: Salford motion capture startup bought by listed firm Posted on September 1, 2026 by staff Salford motion capture startup bought by listed firm Oxford Metrics plc moves for Captive Devices, founded in 2024 by trio of former Epic Games engineers, in deal worth up to £750k Share: Founders MediaTech A Salford motion capture startup has been bought by Oxford Metrics plc. Captive Devices was founded in 2024 by a trio of former Epic Games engineers – including Fred Isaac (pictured) – and received support from GM Business Growth Hub’s Innovation Service in securing innovation grants . A developer of professional head-mounted camera systems and software, it enables markerless facial performance capture, used in visual effects, games and virtual production. Oxford Metrics is a smart sensing and measurement technology group serving life sciences, entertainment, engineering and manufacturing markets. The acquisition adds specialist facial capture to its platform Vicon, which has an established market leadership in body tracking. Captive Devices’ first product was CoreHMC, a head-mounted camera facial motion capture system. The technology captures real human facial expressions and translates them into digital animation data, without the cost or complexity typically associated with bespoke setups. Instead of complicated tailored camera rigs, with custom software builds, time-intensive installation and ongoing technical support, the Captive Devices concept works straight out of the box. Its founding team – who designed and built similar systems prior to founding the business – will be joining Vicon. The startup reported unaudited revenue of £500,000 in the year ended 30th April 2026. Captive Devices’ entire issued share capital is being acquired by the group from Greyhound Industry Ltd, EEInsights Ltd and Periscope Technical Ltd with no debt assumed as part of the transaction. Total consideration for the acquisition is up to £750,000. It comprises of a cash payment of £250,000, issue of Oxford Metrics plc ordinary shares with an aggregate value of £300,000 – allotted quarterly over 24 months – and an earnout of up to £200,000 in cash contingent upon gross profit performance on sales of the facial performance capture system. Imogen O’Connor, CEO of Oxford Metrics, said: “This is exactly the kind of targeted investment we want to make in Vicon – adding differentiated technology and specialist expertise in an area that builds directly on our existing strengths. “Captive Devices extends our capabilities from body tracking into facial performance capture and gives us the opportunity to take proven technology to a much broader global customer base. candidates.lead: Global operations system SafetyCulture is celebrating 10 years of business in Manchester with the biggest transformation in its history, including a rebrand and new AI capabilities.
candidates.evidence_text: SafetyCulture marks 10 years in Manchester with Mitti rebrand and new AI capabilities - Invest Manchester Skip to main content Skip to footer Digital, cyber & AI SafetyCulture marks 10 years in Manchester with Mitti rebrand and new AI capabilities Published on August 21, 2026 News Global operations system SafetyCulture is celebrating 10 years of business in Manchester with the biggest transformation in its history, including a rebrand and new AI capabilities. SafetyCulture today rebrands as Mitti, a new identity signalling its expansion beyond traditional safety management to an all-in-one operations system for the frontline. The word Mitti means “middle” — the centre of an operation, where decisions get made, and work happens. The platform connects the people on the frontline with those making decisions in the boardroom. After launching in Manchester in 2016, Mitti expanded into a 10,000 sq ft office at Bond on Mosley Street in 2024 as its EMEA headquarters. During the decade, Mitti has built a UK customer base of 18,000 organisations, including Unilever, DHL, H&M, Domino’s Pizza, and Network Rail. Celebrating the milestone, Dawid Jaworski, EMEA Lead at Mitti, says : “Ten years ago we were a handful of people in a small Manchester office trying to convince businesses that the clipboard had had its day. A decade on, this city is the base from which we serve the entire EMEA region. “The customers we serve are the industries this region was built on. That proximity matters. Being surrounded by it keeps us honest about who we’re building for. “The city has grown up alongside us. Manchester is now the UK’s largest tech economy outside London with more than 10,000 tech businesses operating here. We built our first decade in Manchester, and we’re building the next one here too.” The platform is used by the workers who don’t sit at a desk — 80%¹ of the world’s workforce — across manufacturing, construction, retail, quick-service restaurants (QSR), energy and other industries. Among its North West customers is Bury-headquartered structural steelwork firm William Hare, which has completed more than 180,000 inspections on the platform, saved over a million sheets of paper, and standardised more than 500 templates across its sites while remaining audit-ready. The rebrand lands as UK operators face a tightening compliance picture. Martyn’s Law will require premises with a capacity of 200 or more to document emergency procedures and train staff accordingly, with enforcement expected from spring 2027. In construction, the Building Safety Act has raised the bar on inspection records, contractor oversight and evidence trails. Jaworski adds : “Every day, more than 3.4 million images and 380,000 inspections are added to our platform — captured by people on site, mid-shift, doing the actual work. That’s ground truth others can’t replicate. It’s the difference between software that guesses what’s happening on the frontline and software that knows.” The tools meant to help teams meet these obligations are falling short, according to Mitti. Only around one-third of frontline supervisors find their digital tools “very effective,” 2 according to a commissioned study conducted by Forrester Consulting on behalf of Mitti. Central to the new Mitti platform is its ‘5 Star Benchmarking’ capability, which turns years of operational history into one clear score for multi-site operators, showing how each location is performing and, more importantly, how to improve. The platform’s new AI capabilities are built on that same frontline data. Agents gather intelligence and automate processes; AI Assistant surfaces patterns and risks, compares performance against relevant standards and regulations, creates action plans and answers questions in seconds. And AI Issue Creation turns a photo, prompt or voice note into a ready-to-review issue. The new two-storey (ground and basement) shop will feature a full floor dedicated to PreLoved items, alongside two accessible fitting rooms and a wheelchair lift As part of the brand’s commitment to championing local creatives, Lucy & Yak has teamed up with Manchester-based illustrator, animator and designer Rick Hyde, who has created a bright, bold and playful artwork piece for the storefront The new store will actually first open its doors to shoppers on Thu 10 Sep, during Manchester Fashion Week, before officially launching with a party and ribbon-cutting on Sat 12 Sep To celebrate, shoppers can enjoy 20% off all day, meet Rick Hyde and see five pieces of his incredible artwork, as well as shop limited-edition totes and tees signed by Rick. candidates.evidence_text: From years spent languishing in post-industrial decline to being crowned one of ‘the coolest neighbourhoods in the world’ 11 April-11 July 2026 View dates and times Date Time Session Features 11 Apr 2026 10:30 am-12:30 pm 11 Jul 2026 10:30 am-12:30 pm Additional information Always double check opening hours with the venue before making a special visit Is there any place in the UK that has changed so quickly and so utterly as Ancoats ? From years spent languishing in post-industrial decline to being crowned one of ‘the coolest neighbourhoods in the world’ in the blink of an eye. What’s the story here? Find out with Jonathan Schofield Tours, with whom you’ll track Ancoats’ changes by strolling its streets, crossing its canals, and taking a look inside one of its most fascinating buildings Starting at Cutting Room Square, your expert tour guide will reveal the layers of history that make Ancoats special, from its place in establishing Manchester’s reputation as ‘Cottonopolis’ to the notorious street gangs, or ‘scuttlers’, who once patrolled and fought here But this winsome stroll is also about the urban regeneration and cultural energy of Ancoats today, which boasts everything from grassroots theatres to Manchester’s only Michelin-starred restaurant

candidates.evidence_text: Manchester Central Library , Manchester Until 20 December 2026 Additional information Always double check opening hours with the venue before making a special visit Manchester has always been a city with stories to tell. This guided walking tour will bring those stories to life. Led by a local expert, the experience is set to be a lively introduction to the people, places and ideas that have shaped one of the UK’s most influential cities The tour will begin at Manchester Central Library, that impossible to miss, grand circular landmark on St Peter’s Square. The neoclassical design has made it one of the city’s most-loved buildings, holding thousands of stories in its walls and on its shelves. The square itself ha From here, the tour takes you through the city’s heart, down the colourful streets of the Gay Village and the calming Sackville Gardens. It is here that you will see the monuments that honour Manchester’s role in the fight for equality and the city’s pioneering LGBTQ+ community a This guided tour is filled with monuments and tales from many moons ago. The Medieval Quarter is the perfect place to soak in all that history. It is here where you will see the oldest public library in the English-speaking world, Chetham’s Library . Housed in a beautiful sandsto During all this walking, your guide will point out local street art, hidden corners and stories you’d easily miss on your own. Tales of suffragettes, reformers, musicians and everyday Mancunians who’ve all left their mark on the city in their own way

candidates.evidence_text: 8 ноября 2026 года в Indigo at The O2 состоится концерт GORAN BREGOVIC в Лондоне Имя Горана Бреговича давно стало символом целого музыкального мира. Его путь начался в многонациональном Сараеве, где восточные мотивы естественно переплетались с западными традициями, а каждая улица имела свой ритм. Именно эта атмосфера сформировала композитора, впоследствии воз Впоследствии музыка Бреговича вышла за рамки концертных площадок. Сотрудничество с режиссером Emir Kusturica подарило мировому кинематографу саундтреки, ставшие неотъемлемой частью фильмов Time of the Gypsies, Arizona Dream и Underground. В этих мелодиях живут Балканы — с их своб Популярность Бреговича родилась не только благодаря знаменитым композициям “Kalashnikov”, “Ederlezi”, “In the Death Car” или “Bella Ciao”. Его главный талант — превращать народные мотивы в современное искусство, не теряя их подлинной силы. Вместе с легендарным “Wedding and Funera Окунитесь в этот балканский водоворот прямо в самом сердце Лондона! Город, который веками принимал выступления и разные культуры со всех континентов, на один вечер станет местом встречи британской сдержанности и безудержной балканской страсти. И, возможно, именно эта неожиданная Чтобы попасть на концерт GORAN BREGOVIC в Лондоне, покупайте билеты на нашем сайте и в кассах города. Еще больше концертов в афише Лондона ищите у нас на сайте

candidates.source_evidence: As AI adoption gathers pace, organisations are under growing pressure to invest and demonstrate where the technology can deliver meaningful business value This lunchtime session brings together senior technology leaders with first-hand experience of putting AI into practice. Drawing on real-world examples and lessons from delivery, the panel will explore what it takes to move from ambition and experimentation to measurable results The discussion will offer a candid view of the decisions, foundations and trade-offs involved. Speakers will share what they have learned from implementing AI, including the technical, operational and organisational challenges encountered along the way There will also be an opportunity to put your questions to the panel and connect with fellow technology leaders over lunch 📅 Date: Thursday 1st October 2026 🕒 Time: 12pm-2pm 📍 Location: No.1 Circle Square 💷 Price: Manchester Digital members - Free (4 x tickets per company) Non members - £30 Spaces are limited - secure your place to gain insight from these senior leaders and connect with peers
candidates.draft_line: • MD Tech Leader Talks 26: From AI ambition to action - delivering measurable ROI — 1 октября, No.1 Circle Square. Уровень: английский и нетворк; Доступ: бесплатно. Почему тебе: профессиональный сигнал по AI/product/fintech/digital transformation; спокойная практика профессионального английского. Действие: зарегистрируйтесь.
